neighbours.label: The Greek letter sigma (σ) inside Greek-script words, vs Greek words that contain no sigma
fire: In the gospel, the word ἐκκλησία is usually translated as church.
The philosophers praised σοφία above wealth.
Sailors feared the stormy θάλασσα in winter.
Plato spoke of the κόσμος as an ordered whole.
The doctor used the Greek νόσος for any illness.
On the map the island was labeled Λέσβος in small letters.
The monks chanted the name Ἰησοῦ at dawn.
Her grandmother still says γιασεμί for jasmine.
quiet: In the gospel, the word ἀγάπη is usually translated as love.
The philosophers praised ἀλήθεια above wealth.
Sailors feared the dark νύχτα in winter.
Plato spoke of the ψυχή as immortal.
The doctor used the Greek καρδιά for the heart.
On the map the island was labeled Κρήτη in small letters.
The monks chanted the word εἰρήνη at dawn.
Her grandmother still says μέλι for honey.

predictions: Greek words containing σ 0.6-1.2; Greek words without σ or ς and Latin-script transliterations under 0.05.
notes: Card: 'σ' x3 in Ασιανή, βασιλεὺς, ἀπόστολος, plus -os/-is endings of transliterated Greek. Probe: βασιλεύς 1.153, Ασία 1.012, ἀπόστολος 0.675; βιβλίο (no sigma) 0.004, Eleusis 0.177, Cyrillic 0.010. Quiet items use Greek words with no σ or final ς.
